citations.desc: Attending veterinarian and adequate veterinary care (dealers and exhibitors).
citations.narrative:
While reviewing APHIS Forms 7005, it was noted that a chocolate colored female poodle (#141, DOB 6/8/21) died on
7/3/26. The licensee stated the dog died from complications during labor. The licensee observed the problem, but never
made contact with the attending veterinarian. Not contacting the attending veterinarian when a dog is having serious
health complications during labor can cause undue suffering for the mom and puppies and cause the death of the adult,
as is the case here. The licensee is required to have a mechanism of direct and frequent communication so that timely
and accurate information on problems of animal health, behavior, and well-being is conveyed to the attending
veterinarian. Correct starting today, 7/27/26.

Three puppies born on 8/31/25 were shipped on 10/21/25. The puppies would have been 51 days old on the day of sale
which is five days shy of the required 8 weeks of age that they are required to be before being transported. Dogs younger
than 8 weeks of age are more susceptible to stresses that occur from travelling and being placed into a new facility. Their
immune systems are more susceptible to becoming compromised which could cause them to become sick and even die.
The licensee must not ship any puppies under 8 weeks of age unless it is directly to the end consumer.

None of the adult dogs have been vaccinated against distemper or parvo in the past year. Not having the adult population
up to date for these vaccinations doesn't ensure they are adequately protected against those diseases. All adult dogs
must be vaccinated for parvo and distemper.
This is a 1st Re-License Inspection for a Class “A” license. The inspection and exit briefing were conducted with the
applicant.
All items must be in compliance within 2 more inspections or by 9/25/26 or the applicant will forfeit the license fee and
must wait 6 months to reapply. Please contact your inspector to schedule your next Re-License Inspection.
Regulated activity can continue under your existing USDA license until it expires.
End of report.
